day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30. No morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Rome Fiumicino Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Take the Leonardo Express train (€14) or a budget bus (€6) to Roma Termini. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Grab a quick late-night snack near the hotel and rest up for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.dinner: Late-night street food near the hotel – look for a nearby pizza al taglio (pizza by the slice) shop or a 24-hour bar for a panino and a drink, budget around €5–8.

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival transfers simple and cheap. The Leonardo Express runs until midnight. Pre-download Google Maps offline for Rome to navigate easily. Exchange or withdraw euros at an ATM at the airport for the best rates.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a classic Roman breakfast at a local bar near the hotel – espresso and a cornetto (croissant) for under €2. Then head to the Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel. Book skip-the-line tickets online in advance (€20–22) to avoid long queues. Spend 3–4 hours exploring one of the world's greatest art collections, including the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and the breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling painted by Michelangelo.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, walk across the Tiber River to visit the exterior of Castel Sant'Angelo (free to view from outside, or €15 to enter – skip entry to stay budget-conscious). Stroll along the scenic Lungotevere riverside promenade. Head to the Trastevere neighborhood for a leisurely afternoon walk through its charming cobblestone streets, colorful buildings, and lively piazzas. Visit the stunning Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere (free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Join the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk to sample local Roman street food including supplì (fried rice balls), cacio e pepe, and local wine while exploring the neighborhood's vibrant nightlife atmosphere with a knowledgeable guide. This is a fantastic budget-friendly way to eat, drink, and discover the neighborhood simultaneously.

meals.breakfast: Espresso and cornetto at a local bar near the hotel – €1.50–2.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick, affordable lunch near the Vatican – try a pizza al taglio slice or a panino from a nearby alimentari (deli). Budget €5–7.
meals.dinner: Covered by the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk. Supplement with a scoop of gelato from a reputable gelateria in Trastevere for €2–3.

day_by_day.notes: Book Vatican Museums tickets well in advance – they sell out fast, especially in June. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Shoulders and knees must be covered to enter the Vatican; bring a scarf or light layer.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, head to the Borghese Gallery Art Experience. Book tickets in advance (€15 + €2 booking fee) – entry is strictly timed (2-hour slots) and sells out weeks ahead. Discover an intimate world-class collection featuring Bernini's dramatic sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's powerful paintings. The gallery is set inside the beautiful Villa Borghese park.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, enjoy a free leisurely stroll through the vast Villa Borghese gardens – Rome's answer to Central Park. Rent a rowboat on the lake (€3–5) or simply relax on the grass. Walk or take a short bus ride to the Spanish Steps (Piazza di Spagna) – free to visit and great for people-watching. Toss a coin in the nearby Trevi Fountain (free) and admire its Baroque grandeur.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the historic centro storico (historic center). Visit the Pantheon at dusk (€5 entry fee, open until 19:00) – one of the best-preserved ancient buildings in the world. Explore the lively Piazza Navona (free) with its Baroque fountains and street artists. Find a budget trattoria in the area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Bar breakfast near the hotel – espresso, cornetto, and fresh-squeezed orange juice. €3–4.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese gardens! Pick up supplies from a nearby alimentari or supermarket – bread, cheese, cured meats, fruit, and a small bottle of water for €6–8 total.
meals.dinner: Budget trattoria near Piazza Navona – look for a fixed-price 'menù del giorno' (menu of the day) which typically includes a first course, second course, and water or house wine for €10–14. Try pasta cacio e pepe or amatriciana.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets are extremely limited – book as early as possible, ideally weeks before arrival. The gallery only allows 360 visitors per 2-hour session. The Pantheon now charges a small entry fee introduced in recent years – confirm current pricing before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, head to the ancient heart of Rome. Join the Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Tour – or visit independently in the morning (combined ticket for Colosseum, Roman Forum & Palatine Hill is €18–20, book online). Explore the Roman Forum, the political and social center of ancient Rome, walking among temples, arches, and the Via Sacra. Climb Palatine Hill for panoramic views over the city and the Circus Maximus.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the iconic Colosseum (included in the combined ticket). Marvel at this 2,000-year-old amphitheater, the largest ever built. After the Colosseum, walk to the nearby Circus Maximus (free to visit exterior) and the Aventine Hill. Visit the Knights of Malta Keyhole (Piazza dei Cavalieri di Malta) – a famous free secret viewpoint where you can see St. Peter's Basilica perfectly framed through a garden keyhole. Explore the beautiful Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) with its sweeping views over Rome.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Trastevere or the Testaccio neighborhood for dinner – Testaccio is considered Rome's culinary heart and is very budget-friendly. Browse the Testaccio Market area (closes in the afternoon but the surrounding streets are lively at night). Enjoy an authentic Roman dinner at a local osteria.

meals.breakfast: Bar breakfast near the hotel – €2–3.
meals.lunch: Street food near the Colosseum – avoid the overpriced tourist traps directly outside. Walk a few blocks to find a pizza al taglio or a supplì bar for €5–7.
meals.dinner: Osteria in Testaccio – try Roman classics like coda alla vaccinara (oxtail stew) or rigatoni alla gricia. Budget €12–16 including house wine.

day_by_day.notes: June in Rome can be very hot – bring a refillable water bottle (Rome has free drinking fountains called 'nasoni' throughout the city) and sunscreen. Start the Colosseum and Forum early to beat the midday heat and crowds. Wear comfortable, sturdy shoes for the uneven ancient cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning to explore at your own pace. Visit the Campo de' Fiori market (open until 14:00, Monday–Saturday) – a lively outdoor market selling fresh produce, flowers, spices, and local goods. Great for picking up affordable snacks and souvenirs. Browse the stalls and soak up the local atmosphere. Then walk to the nearby Jewish Ghetto neighborhood – one of Rome's oldest and most atmospheric districts, with free synagogue exterior views and ancient ruins integrated into the streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Capitoline Hill (Campidoglio) – designed by Michelangelo – for stunning free views over the Roman Forum. Visit the Capitoline Museums (€15), the world's oldest public museums, housing incredible ancient Roman sculptures including the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue and the Capitoline Wolf. Alternatively, save money and simply enjoy the free piazza and viewpoints. Walk down to the Circus Maximus and along the Tiber River.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Pigneto or Ostiense neighborhoods for a more local, off-the-beaten-path evening. These areas are popular with young Romans and offer excellent budget bars, street art, and aperitivo culture. Enjoy a pre-dinner aperitivo (€5–8 for a spritz or glass of wine, often served with free snacks) at a local bar.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh fruit, a pastry, and a coffee at the Campo de' Fiori market – €3–5.
meals.lunch: Affordable lunch in the Jewish Ghetto – try a carciofi alla giudia (Jewish-style fried artichoke) as a snack for €4–6, or find a budget trattoria for a quick pasta dish.
meals.dinner: Budget-friendly restaurant in Pigneto or Ostiense – look for daily specials on a chalkboard menu. Budget €10–14 for a full meal with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Friday evenings in Rome are very lively. The Campo de' Fiori transforms into a popular social gathering spot in the evenings. If visiting the Capitoline Museums, check for free entry days (first Sunday of the month is free for many Rome city museums – though that's Sunday this week, see Day 7).

day_by_day.morning: Visit St. Peter's Basilica in Vatican City – free entry to the basilica itself (€8 to climb the dome for panoramic views, highly recommended). Arrive early (before 09:00) to beat the crowds. Admire Michelangelo's Pietà, Bernini's massive bronze baldachin, and the stunning interior. Climb to the top of the dome for breathtaking 360-degree views over Rome and Vatican City.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Prati neighborhood surrounding the Vatican – a pleasant, slightly upscale residential area with good budget lunch options. In the afternoon, take a leisurely walk along the Tiber River and cross to the other side to explore the Ghetto and Largo di Torre Argentina (free outdoor archaeological site where Julius Caesar was assassinated). Visit the cat sanctuary there – dozens of cats live among the ancient ruins and it's completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Piazza del Popolo area for sunset – the twin Baroque churches and the large piazza are beautiful in the golden hour light (free). Climb the nearby Pincian Hill (accessible by foot or free escalator from the piazza) for one of the best free panoramic views in Rome, especially at sunset. Return to the centro storico for a final evening stroll and dinner.

meals.breakfast: Bar breakfast near the hotel – €2–3. Eat before heading to the Vatican to avoid overpriced options near St. Peter's Square.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Prati – try a local pizzeria or a tavola calda (Italian cafeteria-style restaurant) for a hot meal. Budget €7–10.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for your Saturday night dinner – find a well-reviewed trattoria in the historic center. Try Roman classics: tonnarelli cacio e pepe, saltimbocca alla romana, or tiramisu for dessert. Budget €15–20 with wine.

day_by_day.notes: St. Peter's Basilica has a strict dress code – shoulders and knees must be covered. Security lines can be long on Saturdays; arrive as early as possible. The free views from Pincian Hill are arguably better than the paid Gianicolo viewpoint and are a favorite among locals.

day_by_day.morning: Take advantage of the first Sunday of the month free museum entry – many Rome city-run museums offer free admission on the first Sunday of each month (check current schedules as policies can change). Visit the Capitoline Museums for free if you haven't already, or revisit a favorite site. Alternatively, explore the Porta Portese flea market in Trastevere (Sunday mornings only, until 14:00) – one of Rome's largest and most famous flea markets, great for bargain hunting and people-watching.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your final afternoon revisiting favorite spots, doing any last-minute shopping at budget-friendly stores near Via del Corso, or simply relaxing in a beautiful piazza with a gelato. Visit any remaining must-see sites. Consider a final stroll through Trastevere to say goodbye to your favorite neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farewell dinner at a beloved restaurant you've discovered during the week. Pack your bags and prepare for departure. Depending on your flight time, arrange airport transfer – take the Leonardo Express or a budget bus from Roma Termini back to Fiumicino Airport.

meals.breakfast: A special final Roman breakfast – sit down at a proper bar and enjoy a cappuccino and a fresh maritozzo (cream-filled sweet bun), a Roman specialty. €4–5.
meals.lunch: Light lunch from the Porta Portese market area or a nearby trattoria in Trastevere. Budget €8–10.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at your favorite restaurant discovered during the week, or a new spot near the hotel. Budget €15–18 with wine. End with a final gelato from your favorite gelateria.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight time and plan airport transfer accordingly. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Keep some euros aside for transport to the airport (€6–14 depending on bus or train). The Porta Portese market is cash-only – bring small bills.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Fiumicino Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Leonardo Express train or a pre-booked taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled. If hungry, grab a light snack from a nearby 24-hour bar or the hotel.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light snack at the hotel bar or a nearby late-night café upon arrival — try a tramezzino (Italian sandwich) or a slice of pizza al taglio if available

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — rest is your priority. Set an alarm and prepare for a full first day tomorrow. Confirm any pre-booked experience tickets and download offline maps of Rome.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the hotel, then take a gentle orientation walk along the Tiber River and through the historic center. Stroll across Ponte Sant'Angelo for views of Castel Sant'Angelo and get your first feel for Rome's streets without a packed schedule.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Pantheon (free entry or low-cost timed ticket) and the surrounding Piazza della Rotonda area. Walk to the nearby Piazza Navona to admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers. Browse the piazza's street artists and soak in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Wander into the charming Trastevere neighborhood for dinner. Explore the cobblestone alleys lit by golden evening light before settling in for a relaxed Roman meal.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby cornetto e caffè at a local bar — budget €3–5
meals.lunch: Casual lunch near the Pantheon — try a classic Roman trattoria for cacio e pepe or carbonara, budget €12–18
meals.dinner: Dinner in Trastevere at a mid-range trattoria such as Da Enzo al 29 or similar — try coda alla vaccinara (oxtail stew) and house wine, budget €25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day after your late arrival. Keep the pace relaxed. Wear comfortable walking shoes — Rome's cobblestones can be tough on feet.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel: Start your morning with a pre-booked timed entry (book in advance to skip the long queues). Spend 3–4 hours exploring one of the world's greatest art collections, including the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and the awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling by Michelangelo.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the museums, visit St. Peter's Basilica (free entry) and climb the dome for panoramic views of Rome — budget €8 for the dome climb. Spend the early afternoon exploring St. Peter's Square and the Vatican grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk: Join a guided evening food walk through Trastevere's cobblestone streets, sampling local Roman street food including supplì (fried rice balls), artichokes, and local wines. A perfect way to experience authentic Roman nightlife and cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast near the Vatican — grab a coffee and cornetto at a bar near Prati neighborhood, budget €3–5
meals.lunch: Light lunch in the Prati district near the Vatican — try a pizza bianca with mortadella or a quick panino, budget €8–12
meals.dinner: Included in the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk experience — tastings of multiple street foods and wines

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums tickets should be booked well in advance, especially for June (peak season). Dress code applies for St. Peter's Basilica — shoulders and knees must be covered. The evening food walk typically lasts 2.5–3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market & Cooking Class: Head to Rome's most authentic local food market — Testaccio Market — where locals and professional chefs shop daily. Browse stalls of fresh produce, cheeses, cured meats, and Roman specialties before joining a hands-on cooking class to learn how to make traditional Roman dishes from scratch.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cooking class (typically ending early-to-mid afternoon), walk off your meal exploring the Testaccio neighborhood — one of Rome's most authentic working-class districts. Visit the Non-Catholic Cemetery (Cimitero Acattolico) where Keats and Shelley are buried, and see the ancient Pyramid of Cestius nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Relax with an aperitivo hour — find a rooftop bar or enoteca for a Campari spritz or Aperol spritz with complimentary nibbles. Then enjoy a quieter evening strolling along the Tiber or revisiting a favorite neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast included or grab coffee near Testaccio before the market visit, budget €3–5
meals.lunch: Lunch is typically included as part of the cooking class experience — you eat what you cook!
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at an enoteca (wine bar with food) in the Testaccio or Trastevere area — cheese and charcuterie boards, bruschetta, and a carafe of local wine, budget €20–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Testaccio Market & Cooking Class usually runs from morning into early afternoon (roughly 4–5 hours). Confirm exact timings when booking. Testaccio is also famous for its offal-based Roman cuisine — adventurous eaters should try the local specialties at the market stalls.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Experience: Visit the intimate and world-class Galleria Borghese, featuring Bernini's breathtaking sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and masterpieces by Caravaggio. Entry is strictly timed and limited to 2 hours — book tickets well in advance as this is one of Rome's most sought-after experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, stroll through the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens — Rome's central park. Rent a rowboat on the small lake, relax on the grass, or walk to the Pincio Terrace for one of the best panoramic views over Rome's rooftops and St. Peter's dome. Explore the nearby Piazza del Popolo.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Spanish Steps area for early evening people-watching. Walk the Via Condotti (Rome's luxury shopping street) for window shopping, then find a mid-range restaurant in the area for dinner. End the evening with a gelato from a quality gelateria.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near the Borghese Gallery, budget €4–6
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in Villa Borghese gardens — pick up fresh bread, cheese, prosciutto, and fruit from a nearby deli or alimentari, budget €10–15
meals.dinner: Dinner near the Spanish Steps or Piazza del Popolo — try a mid-range Roman restaurant for rigatoni all'amatriciana and tiramisu, budget €25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets must be booked in advance — same-day availability is almost impossible in June. The gallery only admits a limited number of visitors every 2 hours. Combine the visit with a leisurely afternoon in the gardens to make the most of the area.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Tour (morning visit): Begin at the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill — the ancient heart of Rome. Walk through the ruins where emperors once ruled, explore the Via Sacra, the Arch of Titus, and climb Palatine Hill for sweeping views over the Forum. Combine your ticket with the Colosseum (included in the same ticket).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Colosseum for a self-guided or audio-guided tour of the iconic amphitheater. Afterward, explore the Celio neighborhood nearby — a quieter, leafy area with beautiful churches including the Basilica di San Clemente, which has three layers of history descending underground.
day_by_day.evening: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Tour (evening option): If the experience offers an evening/sunset slot, opt for this magical time when the golden hour light bathes the ancient ruins. Alternatively, enjoy a farewell-style dinner in the charming Monti neighborhood — Rome's hipster village — full of independent restaurants, wine bars, and boutiques.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at a bar near the Colosseum area, budget €3–5
meals.lunch: Lunch in the Monti neighborhood — try a casual osteria for a plate of pasta and house wine, budget €14–20
meals.dinner: Dinner in Monti at a lively mid-range restaurant — try abbacchio alla romana (Roman-style lamb) or a seasonal vegetable dish, with local Frascati wine, budget €25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Colosseum and Roman Forum tickets in advance — long queues are common in June. The combined ticket covers the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill. If the Palatine Hill Sunset Tour experience offers a guided evening slot, prioritize that for a dramatically beautiful experience.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a relaxed final breakfast. Take a slow morning walk to any neighborhoods or sites you want to revisit — perhaps the Campo de' Fiori morning market for a lively local scene, or a final espresso at a classic Roman bar standing at the counter like a local.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping — explore artisan shops in the centro storico for quality Italian goods: leather goods, ceramics, olive oils, or local wines. Visit any remaining churches or piazzas on your list. Head back to the hotel to collect luggage and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a restaurant that has stood out during your trip, or try something new — a classic Roman pizzeria for a crispy Roman-style pizza (pizza al taglio or pizza tonda). Raise a final glass of Italian wine to the Eternal City before heading to the airport or retiring for an early next-day flight.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast or a beloved neighborhood café, budget €4–8
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Campo de' Fiori or a nearby alimentari — a fresh sandwich, olives, and a cold drink, budget €8–12
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a favorite trattoria or a classic Roman pizzeria — pizza Margherita, supplì, and a cold Peroni or local wine, budget €20–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Allow plenty of travel time to the airport — Rome's traffic can be unpredictable, especially in summer. The Leonardo Express from Termini to Fiumicino takes about 32 minutes and runs frequently. Factor in at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security.

day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, take a scenic walk through the Villa Borghese gardens. Head to the elegant Parioli or Spagna neighborhood for a long, indulgent Roman lunch. Then explore the Spanish Steps, Via Condotti luxury boutiques, and the Trevi Fountain at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to freshen up. Enjoy a sunset aperitivo on the hotel terrace or a nearby rooftop bar with views over Rome. Dinner at a refined Roman restaurant — white tablecloths, candlelight, and exceptional Roman cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — eggs, pastries, fresh fruit, cappuccino on the terrace
meals.lunch: Il Sorpasso or Ristorante Mirabelle (rooftop, near Via Veneto) — cacio e pepe, artichokes alla romana, and a chilled Vermentino
meals.dinner: La Pergola (Rome's only 3-Michelin-star restaurant, atop the Rome Cavalieri hotel) — tasting menu with wine pairing; advance reservation essential

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery requires advance timed-entry booking — confirm reservation before travel. La Pergola reservations should be made weeks in advance. Private car recommended for all transfers today.

day_by_day.morning: Early private transfer to the Vatican for the Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel skip-the-line experience. A private expert guide leads you through the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and into the awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel. Early entry ensures smaller crowds and an unhurried, premium experience. Optionally add a private papal audience or St. Peter's Basilica rooftop access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lunch in the Prati neighborhood near the Vatican — Rome's best kept local secret for excellent trattorias. After lunch, cross the Tiber to explore Castel Sant'Angelo at your own pace, with stunning views over the Tiber River. Optional: private guided tour of Castel Sant'Angelo's secret papal apartments.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — join an expert local guide through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere, sampling supplì (Roman rice balls), artisanal cheeses, cured meats, and local wines at hidden enotecas and market stalls. The perfect sensory introduction to authentic Roman food culture.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — early start recommended; grab a cornetto and espresso at the hotel bar if departing before 8:00
meals.lunch: Osteria dell'Angelo (Prati) — classic Roman trattoria beloved by locals; rigatoni all'amatriciana and abbacchio (Roman lamb)
meals.dinner: Included in the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk experience; supplement with a final glass of wine at a candlelit Trastevere wine bar such as Enoteca Ferrara

day_by_day.notes: Vatican entry requires strict timed booking — confirm skip-the-line private tour well in advance. Dress code enforced at St. Peter's Basilica (covered shoulders and knees). The Trastevere walk typically runs 3–3.5 hours from early evening.

day_by_day.morning: Hotel breakfast, then a private transfer to Testaccio for the Testaccio Market & Cooking Class experience. Begin at Rome's most authentic food market — browse stalls of seasonal produce, aged cheeses, fresh pasta, and offal with a local chef guide. Then move to a premium cooking studio for a hands-on class mastering Roman classics: carbonara, cacio e pepe, and a seasonal dessert.
day_by_day.afternoon: After your cooking class lunch, take a digestive walk through the Testaccio neighborhood — explore the Monte dei Cocci (ancient amphora hill), street art, and the Non-Catholic Cemetery (where Keats and Shelley are buried). Return to the hotel mid-afternoon for pool time, spa, or simply relax on the beachfront.
day_by_day.evening: Elegant dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant or a nearby fine dining establishment. Enjoy the evening ambiance of the resort — perhaps a cocktail on the beach terrace as the sun sets over the Mediterranean.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Included in the Testaccio Cooking Class — you eat what you cook; paired with regional Italian wines
meals.dinner: Aroma Restaurant (rooftop of Palazzo Manfredi, overlooking the Colosseum) — seasonal Roman fine dining with one of the most dramatic views in the city; alternatively, the hotel's own premium restaurant for a relaxed evening

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class typically runs from morning through a 13:00–14:00 lunch. Comfortable, closed-toe shoes recommended for the market. Book Aroma Restaurant in advance if choosing that option.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to the ancient heart of Rome for the Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Tour — though today, take the morning slot for cooler temperatures and softer light. A private archaeologist guide brings the ruins to life: the Forum where Caesar walked, the Arch of Titus, and the imperial palaces of Palatine Hill with sweeping views over the city. Optionally add the Colosseum with arena floor access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lunch in the Celio or Monti neighborhood — Rome's hippest historic quarter. Spend the afternoon exploring Monti's artisan boutiques, vintage shops, and hidden piazzas. Visit the Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore and the lesser-known but spectacular Basilica of San Clemente (three layers of history underground). Return to hotel for a late afternoon rest or spa treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo at a rooftop terrace bar in central Rome (Terrazza Borromini or Il Giardino Rooftop at the Sina Bernini Bristol offer spectacular views). Followed by dinner in the atmospheric centro storico.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Ristorante Urbana 47 (Monti) — farm-to-table Roman cuisine using hyper-local ingredients; excellent natural wine list
meals.dinner: Il Pagliaccio (2 Michelin stars, centro storico) — innovative Italian tasting menu; one of Rome's most celebrated fine dining experiences; advance reservation essential

day_by_day.notes: Morning visits to the Forum are strongly recommended over sunset in summer heat (June temperatures can reach 32–35°C). Wear comfortable walking shoes — the ancient site involves uneven cobblestones. Colosseum arena floor access requires separate premium booking.

day_by_day.morning: A slower, self-directed morning. Hotel breakfast, then a private guided tour of a lesser-visited Roman gem: the Palazzo Doria Pamphilj (home to a stunning private art collection including Velázquez's portrait of Pope Innocent X) or the Capitoline Museums — the world's oldest public museums with extraordinary Roman sculpture and panoramic views of the Forum. Alternatively, arrange a private studio visit with a contemporary Roman artist through the hotel concierge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a long Roman lunch in the Pantheon neighborhood. After lunch, visit the Pantheon itself (free entry, book timed slot) and wander the Piazza Navona area. Treat yourself to artisanal gelato at Giolitti or Della Palma. Optional: a private fashion consultation or tailoring appointment on Via Condotti or Via del Babuino for a luxury souvenir.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-eve celebration dinner — reserve a private dining room or chef's table experience for an unforgettable final full evening in Rome. Return to the hotel for a nightcap on the beachfront terrace under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — request a special spread if celebrating
meals.lunch: Ristorante Fortunato al Pantheon — a Roman institution since 1975, beloved by politicians and artists; classic Roman cuisine steps from the Pantheon
meals.dinner: Imàgo at Hotel Hassler (rooftop, Spanish Steps) — panoramic Rome skyline, exceptional tasting menu, world-class wine cellar; the ultimate splurge dinner in Rome

day_by_day.notes: Palazzo Doria Pamphilj is often overlooked by tourists and offers an extraordinary, crowd-free art experience. The Pantheon now requires a timed entry ticket (book online). Imàgo and Il Pagliaccio are both exceptional — choose based on preference; do not double-book on the same trip without comparing notes.

day_by_day.morning: Final hotel breakfast — linger over your cappuccino and cornetto. Depending on your departure time, enjoy one last walk along the beachfront or a morning swim. For a meaningful final morning in the city, arrange a private early visit to a Roman church of your choice (Santa Maria in Aracoeli, Sant'Ignazio di Loyola, or the Baths of Diocletian) before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Private luxury transfer to Rome Fiumicino Airport. Arrive with ample time for the premium terminal experience — use the Lufthansa or Alitalia business lounge, or the independent Sala Monteverdi lounge at FCO. Browse duty-free for last-minute Roman provisions: truffle products, aged Parmigiano, or a bottle of Barolo.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Rome with extraordinary memories of art, food, history, and la dolce vita.

meals.breakfast: Final full hotel breakfast — savor every bite
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the hotel or a quick stop at a high-end Roman deli (Roscioli Salumeria or Volpetti in Testaccio) for gourmet takeaway provisions for the journey
meals.dinner: Airport lounge or on-board dining (request the premium meal option in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the hotel — request late checkout if your flight departs in the evening. Pack any perishable food purchases (cheeses, cured meats) in checked luggage according to airline and customs regulations. Tip your private driver and guide generously — they have been the unsung heroes of your Roman holiday.
